notes: The whole 42-page adopted PDF, read end to end: the preface and contributors, the introduction, the historic context (Native Americans and colonization, the Mexican era, the Gold Rush, urban expansion, the advent of the Gilded Age, early built environment characteristics), the Existing City Landmarks list, the three style themes (Greek Revival 1848-1885, Gothic Revival 1848-1906, Folk Victorian 1865-1906) with their narratives, evaluation criteria, eligibility standards, character-defining features and integrity considerations, the Early Vernacular section, all 24 figures, and the bibliography. There is no inventory table and no APN anywhere in the document. The dense seams are the Existing City Landmarks list on pp. 16-17, which gives a landmark number, an address, a style and a year for each of thirteen properties, the Religious Structures list on p. 29, which gives eight more churches with addresses and years, and the figure captions.

coverage.remaining: None. The document was read in full; nothing in it is outstanding.
coverage.note: 31 numbered-address mentions across 42 pages, resolving to 30 distinct street addresses; St. Patrick's Church is printed both as 756 Mission Street in the landmark list and as 748-756 Mission Street in the Fig. 15 caption, and carries two findings because the caption states a separate dated event (the 1906 destruction and the rebuild without the steeple). Two of the addresses are buildings the statement itself calls non-extant: 555 Harrison Street and 37 Sterling. Four more buildings are named with no street number at all and are not recorded as findings: the Old United States Mint given only as '5th and Mission Streets' in the narrative (its landmark-list entry supplies 88 Fifth Street), the Yerba Buena Island Light Station Keeper's Quarters of 1873, the cottages on Napier Lane of circa 1875-1890, and the Sutro Baths. The statement contradicts itself on three build years: Old St. Patrick's Church (circa 1854 versus circa 1852), the Nightengale House (1882 versus 1878) and the Old Mint (1874 versus circa 1869); each is recorded on the finding's conflict field, unadjudicated. It also prints the Feusier Octagon House as 1607 Green Street where the department's own Victorian Era Styles statement prints 1067 Green Street.

The statement says it could be found eligible under Criterion C/3.

findings.description: St. John Prodromos Greek Orthodox Church and the Alexander the Great Meeting Hall stood here, photographed in 1919 and shown for their Greek Revival full-width columned porch. The building is no longer extant; the statement places the site near what is now the Bryant Street onramp to the Bay Bridge.
